name: Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump
description: In southwest Alberta, where the Rocky Mountain foothills rise from the prairie, this cliff was used for nearly 6,000 years by Plains peoples to hunt bison. Hunters drove herds along marked trails and over the edge, then butchered the animals at a camp below. You can still see the drive lanes and thick deposits of bison bones, and a museum of Blackfoot culture now stands on the site.
